purpose: Add family entanglements and restoration-role motifs around Osiris, Horus, Anubis, Seth, Nephthys, Isis and Imhotep without collapsing different periods or traditions into one genealogy.

heliopolitan_ennead_core.source_note: British Museum educational summary explicitly lists Geb and Nut as parents of Osiris, Isis, Seth and Nephthys.

details: Plutarch states that Isis bore Horus lawfully while Nephthys bore Anubis clandestinely.
Plutarch later states that Isis treated Anubis as if he were her own child.

son_function_B.genealogical_note: Treat 'son of Osiris' only in the late Plutarchian lineage layer; Anubis's funerary role is broader and older than that late genealogy.

secure_relations: SETH and OSIRIS are brothers in the Ennead family
SETH and NEPHTHYS are spouses in major later narrative traditions
HORUS is therefore Seth's nephew in the Osirian succession story
late_narrative_entanglement: Anubis born from that union in Plutarch's account
Isis accepts/raises Anubis in Plutarch's account
SETH_FAMILY_ENTANGLEMENT_MOTIFS.claim_ceiling: These are narrative/family motifs. Do not state that adultery was the historically primary Egyptian reason Seth killed Osiris unless a specific source says so in the tested textual layer.

not_osiris_son.statement: Do not model deified Imhotep as a son of Osiris.

evidence_notes: Met statuette inscription describes Imhotep as eldest son of Ptah.
British Museum EA63800 calls him 'the Great One, son of the god Ptah'.
UCL bronze inscription gives Imhotep as son of Ptah.
Met identifies Khereduankh as the mother of Imhotep in late beliefs.
Met 89.2.528 reads 'eldest son of Ptah' and 'born of Cherduankh'.
UCL LDUCE-UC16444 reads Imhotep, son of Ptah, born of Kheredankh.

IMHOTEP_GENEALOGY_FIREWALL.sekhmet_warning: Do not freeze SEKHMET as Imhotep's mother from modern summaries alone. The museum inscriptions used in this pass support Khereduankh; any Sekhmet genealogy requires its own source-specific node.

functional_bridge_to_osiris.allowed: IMHOTEP_RESTORATION/HEALING/CULT_FUNCTION <-> OSIRIAN_RESTORATION_MOTIF as a functional homolog
functional_bridge_to_osiris.forbidden: IMHOTEP = SON_OF_OSIRIS or IMHOTEP = OSIRIS without independent evidence

ADDITIONAL_FAMILY_MOTIFS_FOR_JANUS.use: When a source speaks of restoration, ask which layer is meant: dynastic/social, anatomical/funerary, or both.
Separate kinship relation from political/ritual role.

ADDITIONAL_FAMILY_MOTIFS_FOR_JANUS.graph: NEPHTHYS[SETH_HOUSE] + OSIRIS -> ANUBIS -> joins Isis/Osiris funerary restoration network
ADDITIONAL_FAMILY_MOTIFS_FOR_JANUS.use: Potential narrative motif for custody transfer across rival family branches; not early-Egyptian proof.

ADDITIONAL_FAMILY_MOTIFS_FOR_JANUS.graph: ROLE(ANUBIS)=EMBALM/GUARD can be analytically useful even when genealogical parentage varies
ADDITIONAL_FAMILY_MOTIFS_FOR_JANUS.use: Prefer role continuity over forced genealogy in reverse semantic passes.
Keep Imhotep in the search as a restoration-function/cult-office bridge, not as an invented Osiris son.

REVERSE_SEARCH_IMPLICATIONS.old_question: Is person X literally a son/relative of Osiris?
REVERSE_SEARCH_IMPLICATIONS.new_question: Which family role carries which restoration function, and can that role predict a source-bearing ritual/material relation?
preferred_queries: SETH + adversary/brother/uncle roles without collapsing all motives
IMHOTEP + Ptah genealogy + restoration/healing/cult function, separately from Osiris kinship

SOURCE_LEDGER.source: British Museum, Ancient Egyptian gods and goddesses
SOURCE_LEDGER.supports: Geb + Nut -> Osiris, Isis, Seth, Nephthys

SOURCE_LEDGER.source: Plutarch, De Iside et Osiride, late Greco-Roman witness
SOURCE_LEDGER.supports: Isis gives birth to Horus lawfully; Nephthys bears Anubis clandestinely; Isis later treats Anubis as her own
Imhotep = eldest son of Ptah; born of Cherduankh/Khereduankh
Khereduankh = mother of Imhotep in late beliefs

SOURCE_LEDGER.source: UCL Petrie Museum bronze Imhotep figure
SOURCE_LEDGER.supports: Imhotep, son of Ptah, born of Kheredankh
Imhotep epithet: son of the god Ptah

canonical_seal: DO NOT FORCE ONE FAMILY TREE ACROSS THREE MILLENNIA. KEEP GENEALOGY LAYERED, BUT USE THE ROLE SPLIT: HORUS RESTORES THE FATHER'S ORDER; ANUBIS RESTORES AND GUARDS THE FATHER'S BODY; IMHOTEP REMAINS A FUNCTIONAL RESTORATION BRIDGE, NOT AN INVENTED SON OF OSIRIS.
